sessions.empty: No sessions recorded yet. The launcher measures memory while the game runs and keeps the last {{kept}} sessions here.

sessions.partial: The launcher lost track of the game part way through, so this session is incomplete.
sessions.unreadable: These sessions could not be read, so the launcher has left the file alone.
sessions.unreadableRecovery: Clearing them removes the file, and the launcher starts recording again from the next session.
sessions.newerFormat: These sessions were recorded by a newer version of the launcher, so the launcher has left the file alone.
sessions.chartLabel: Memory and CPU across one session, peaking at {{peak}} over {{duration}}.
sessions.chartLegend: Memory is the solid line, peaking at {{peak}}. CPU is the dashed line.
sessions.chartLegendMemoryOnly: Memory is the solid line, peaking at {{peak}}. CPU is not measured on this system.
sessions.tableCaption: Every reading taken during this session.
sessions.steadyClimb: Memory only went up during this session.
sessions.steadyClimbMeaning: The launcher measures the whole game from outside, so this cannot say what used the memory. A mod, the game itself and a large world all look the same from here. Comparing sessions with different mods enabled is what narrows it down.

mods.profilesIntro: A profile is a named set of the Mods that are on. Using one turns Mods on and off until this Installation's Mods folder matches it. Nothing is copied or downloaded. While a profile is in use it follows the folder: turning Mods on or off, installing or deleting them changes that profile.

config.wrongtwofa: That 2FA code is incorrect or expired. Check your authenticator and try again.
config.requiresTwoFA: This account requires a 2FA code. Enter the code from your authenticator and try again.
config.invalidEmailPass: Invalid email or password. Log in with the account's email address, not the player name.
config.loginUnreachable: Couldn't reach the login service. Check your connection or firewall and try again.
config.accountRestricted: The account service refused this login. If the account is banned or locked, check the email Vintage Story sent for details.
config.serviceError: The login service answered with an error on its side. Try again in a few minutes.
config.certificateError: The login service's secure connection couldn't be verified. A firewall or antivirus inspecting secure traffic can cause this.
config.networkUnreachable: Couldn't reach the login service. Check your connection, or a proxy if your network uses one, then try again.
config.noKeyring: No system keyring was found to store the session. On Linux that is GNOME Keyring or KWallet, and the guide below explains how to set one up.
config.sessionNotRemembered: You are logged in, but no system keyring was found to store the session, so it lasts only until you close RiftLauncher. On Linux the keyring is GNOME Keyring or KWallet, and the guide below explains how to set one up.
config.unexpectedResponse: The account service answered in a way this launcher couldn't read. Your password was not rejected. Try again after an update.
config.sessionStoreUnreadable: Your login worked, but the saved-accounts file can't be read and couldn't be backed up, so the launcher left it alone rather than overwrite it. Nothing was saved this time.
config.sessionStoreRebuilt: The saved-accounts file couldn't be read. A copy was kept and the launcher started a fresh one, so any other accounts on this device need to log in again.
config.onlyIfEnabledTwoFA: Only if your account uses 2FA. Used for this login only.
config.loginPrivacySent: RiftLauncher sends your email, password, and optional 2FA code to the official Vintage Story account service over HTTPS.
config.loginPrivacyStored: Your password and 2FA code are not saved by RiftLauncher. Your account profile and session data stay on this device so you do not need to log in again. You can remove the account from the account menu.
config.loginPrivacyGame: When you launch the game, the session data Vintage Story needs is written to the selected installation.
config.receiveBetaUpdatesDesc: Toggle on to be offered beta versions of the launcher when it checks for updates. Turning it off while you are on a beta stops the next ones being offered and keeps the one you have until a stable release arrives.
config.backgroundsLoadFailed: The background list couldn't be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
config.areYouSureRemoveAccount: Are you sure you want to remove {{user}}?
config.removeAccountNotReversible: Removing an account is not reversible but you can add it back again by logging in with the same Vintage Story account again.

moddbVisibility.title: Help other players find RiftLauncher
moddbVisibility.body: RiftLauncher is listed on ModDB, where every version has its own entry and its own download count, and those counts are most of what decides whether anyone finds the launcher. If you want to help, the launcher can ask ModDB once for this version's entry, which registers as one download there. The entry holds a 315 byte text file pointing at the releases page, not the launcher itself, and the launcher does not keep it. Nothing is installed and nothing else changes.
